What happens to my Yahoo Mail when I die?

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 26 Oct 2026

Short answer: Yahoo won't hand over a password, and accounts can't be transferred, even after death. For US accounts, family can ask Yahoo to close the account or stop billing with a US death certificate. Getting the content needs a US court order. Yahoo's help page says it applies to US accounts only and it won't respond to non-US requests.

Key facts

  • No passwords or login details released
  • Accounts are non-transferable
  • US accounts: closure needs a US death certificate
  • Content: US court order required

How do I prepare my Yahoo Mail account?

  1. Store your Yahoo password and recovery details in a password manager with emergency access, because Yahoo won't release them.
  2. Forward or export important emails and attachments you'd want kept.
  3. List the account and any paid Yahoo services in your digital estate plan.
  4. After a death (US accounts): use Yahoo's deceased-user forms to close the account or cancel billing and premium services, uploading a US-issued death certificate.
  5. Need the emails? Yahoo requires a US court order meeting its requirements, plus the death certificate and your government ID. Get legal advice.
  6. Outside the US: Yahoo's page says it won't accept these requests, so check Yahoo Help for your region and stop payments through the bank.

Read the official policy ↗

What documents do heirs need?

  • To close or stop billing: the person's full name, Yahoo email, date of death and a US-issued death certificate
  • For content: also your government ID and a US court order

How long does it take?

Yahoo publishes no processing time. It reviews each request and contacts you if it needs more information.

What can't be recovered?

  • Email content, unless a court order succeeds
  • Everything in the account once it's closed

Frequently asked questions

What happens to my Yahoo Mail when I die?

Yahoo won't hand over a password, and accounts can't be transferred, even after death. For US accounts, family can ask Yahoo to close the account or stop billing with a US death certificate. Getting the content needs a US court order. Yahoo's help page says it applies to US accounts only and it won't respond to non-US requests.

Can I get into a dead person's Yahoo Mail?

Yahoo says it can't provide passwords or login details, and accounts are non-transferable. Content requests need a US court order.

How do I close a deceased person's Yahoo account?

For US accounts, submit Yahoo's closure form with the person's name, Yahoo email, date of death and a US-issued death certificate.

What if the person lived outside the US?

Yahoo's page says it applies to US accounts only and won't respond to non-US requests. Check Yahoo Help for your region, and stop charges through the bank.

How do I stop Yahoo charging a dead person's card?

For US accounts, use Yahoo's form to suspend or cancel billing and premium services. Without a death certificate, Yahoo says to call Yahoo Customer Service on 866-265-4025.
